en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 1.3.
Vedanāttika (The Triplet on Feeling)
Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra): Root Condition (Hetu).
Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling, there arises a state associated with pleasant feeling.
By way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, there arise two aggregates; dependent on two aggregates, there arises one aggregate.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, there arise two aggregates;
dependent on two aggregates, there arises one aggregate.
Dependent on a state associated with painful feeling, a state associated with painful feeling arises by way of the root condition:
dependent on one aggregate associated with painful feeling, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].
Dependent on a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, there arises a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of root condition:

dependent on one aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, two aggregates arise; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking, [dependent on one aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling...]
In dependence on one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise]; in dependence on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].
Regarding the object and so forth:
in dependence on a state associated with pleasant feeling, a state associated with pleasant feeling arises.

By way of object condition … by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*; there is no rebirth-linking through predominance) … by way of proximity condition … by way of contiguity condition … by way of conascence condition … by way of mutuality condition … by way of support condition … by way of decisive support condition … by way of prenascence condition—
one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, in dependence upon which, two aggregates [arise].
Dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]. [Dependent on] the basis, by way of prenascence condition. (Abbreviated.
Regarding repetition, etc.:
dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling, a state associated with pleasant feeling arises.
By way of repetition-condition … by way of kamma-condition … by way of result-condition: dependent on one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise];

dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise]; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].
Dependent on a state associated with painful feeling, a state associated with painful feeling arises by way of resultant condition:
dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pain and accompanied by body-consciousness, two aggregates arise;
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises.
Dependent on a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, there arises a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of resultant condition:

dependent on one aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise]; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]; at the moment of rebirth-linking, [dependent on] one aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling...
In dependence on one aggregate associated with feeling, two aggregates [arise]; in dependence on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].
Regarding nutriment and so forth:
in dependence on a state associated with pleasant feeling, a state associated with pleasant feeling arises.
Conditioned by nutriment … conditioned by faculty … conditioned by jhāna … conditioned by path … conditioned by association … conditioned by dissociation:
dependent on one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise];

dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]; [dependent on] the physical basis, [there is arising] by way of dissociation condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, [dependent on] pleasant feeling …
In dependence on one aggregate associated with feeling, two aggregates [arise]; in dependence on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].
[This is] by way of dissociation condition (*vippayuttapaccaya*) with respect to the basis (*vatthu*).
In dependence on a state associated with painful feeling, a state associated with painful feeling [arises].
[It] arises by way of dissociation condition: dependent on one aggregate associated with painful feeling, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]. [Also] the physical basis [arises] by way of dissociation condition.
Dependent on a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, [arises] a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling...
A state arises by way of dissociation condition: dependent on one aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]; the physical basis [arises] by way of dissociation condition;
at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, two [aggregates arise].
Aggregates: one aggregate in dependence on two aggregates. [The relationship of] dissociation with respect to the physical basis. (Abbreviated.
Presence, etc.:
by way of presence condition … absence condition … disappearance condition … non-disappearance condition …
In the Pure Enumeration Chapter,
there are three for root-cause, three for object … pe … and three for non-disappearance.

With root condition (*hetu-paccaya*), there are three [answers] for the object condition (*ārammaṇa*), ... pe ... two for the result condition (*vipāka*), ... pe ... three for the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*), ... pe ....

With object condition and predominance condition (*adhipati-paccaya*), there are three for the root condition, ... pe ... two for the result condition, ... pe ... three for the non-disappearance condition, ... pe ....

By way of repetition-condition (*āsevanapaccaya*), there are three [results] with root-cause (*hetu*) …pe… three with kamma … three with nutriment (*āhāra*) …pe… three with non-disappearance (*avigata*) …pe….

By way of resultant-condition (*vipākapaccaya*), there are two with root-cause, three with object (*ārammaṇa*), two with predominance (*adhipati*) …pe… three with prenascence (*purejāta*), three with kamma …pe… two with jhāna, two with path (*magga*) …pe… three with non-disappearance …pe….
By way of jhāna-condition (*jhānapaccaya*), there are three with root-cause …pe… two with resultant …pe… three with non-disappearance …pe….
With path-condition, there are three [instances] for root-condition … pe … two for resultant-condition … pe … three for non-disappearance-condition … pe ….
With non-disappearance-condition, there are three for root-condition … pe … three for absence-condition, three for disappearance-condition … pe ….
Just as the enumeration of conditions for the wholesome triad, so should it be expanded in detail.
1.3.1.2. Analysis of the Negative Section on Conditions (Paccayapaccanīya Vibhaṅgavāra):
Not-root (Nahetu)
Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling, a state associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of the not-root condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, two aggregates arise;
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises.
Dependent on a state associated with painful feeling, a state associated with painful feeling arises by way of the not-root condition:
dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pain and accompanied by body-consciousness, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].

Dependent on a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, there arises a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of the not-root condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]; at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking...
In dependence on one aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise];

in dependence on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]; and in dependence on the aggregates associated with doubt and associated with restlessness, delusion associated with doubt and associated with restlessness [arises].

Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling through the condition of not being a predominance, there arises a state associated with pleasant feeling through the condition of not being a predominance. (The full treatment of non-predominance including rebirth-linking.
Non-prenascence.
Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling, a state associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of not-prenascence condition:
in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling...
Dependent on one aggregate, two aggregates [arise]; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].

Dependent on a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises by way of not-prenascence condition: in the formless realm, dependent on one [aggregate] associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling...

Dependent on one aggregate, two aggregates [arise]; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise]; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].
Not by way of posteriority or repetition.
Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling, a state associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of neither-postnascence condition nor-repetition condition.
(The postnascence and repetition conditions are both complete for rebirth-linking.
Not-kamma.
Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling, a state associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of not-kamma condition:
dependent on aggregates associated with pleasant feeling, volition associated with pleasant feeling arises.
Dependent on a state associated with painful feeling, a state associated with painful feeling [arises]...
A state associated with painful feeling arises by way of the not-kamma condition dependent on aggregates associated with painful feeling; dependent on volition associated with painful feeling.

A state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises by way of the not-kamma condition dependent on a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; dependent on aggregates associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
Volition associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling that is neither-resultant-nor-jhāna, there arises a state associated with pleasant feeling.
...arises by way of non-resultant condition … by way of non-jhāna condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pleasure and accompanied by body-consciousness, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].
Dependent on a state associated with painful feeling, a state associated with painful feeling [arises].
It arises by way of non-jhāna condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pain and accompanied by body-consciousness, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].
Dependent on a state associated with neither-pain-nor-pleasure feeling, [arises] a state associated with neither-pain-nor-pleasure feeling.
A state arises not by way of jhāna condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by fourfold consciousness, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].
Not-path.
Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling, a state associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of not-path condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].
Dependent on a state associated with painful feeling, a state associated with painful feeling arises by way of not-path condition:
dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pain and accompanied by body-consciousness, two aggregates arise;
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises.

Dependent on a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, there arises a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of not-path condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]; at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking...
In dependence on one aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, there are two aggregates;
in dependence on two aggregates, there is one aggregate.
Non-dissociation.
Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling, a state associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of non-dissociation condition:
in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise];
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].

Dependent on a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, there arises a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of non-dissociation condition: in the formless realm, dependent on one aggregate associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, two aggregates arise;
dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises.
In the Enumeration Chapter (Saṅkhyāvāra), under the Pure (Suddha) section:

with not-root (na-hetu) there are three; with not-predominance (na-adhipati) there are three; with not-prenascence (na-purejāta) there are two; with not-postnascence (na-pacchājāta) there are three; with not-repetition (na-āsevana) there are three; with not-kamma (na-kamma) there are three; with not-resultant (na-vipāka) there are three; with not-jhāna (na-jhāna) there are three; with not-path (na-magga) there are three; with not-dissociation (na-vippayutta) there are two.
1.2. Analysis of the Negative Section on Conditions:
The Non-root Dyad (Nahetuduka)

With not-root condition, there are three [results] with not-predominance; one with not-prenascence; three with not-postnascence; three with not-repetition; two with not-kamma; two with not-resultant; three with not-jhāna; three with not-path; one with not-dissociation …pe…. Fourfold Combination:

With not-root condition, not-predominance condition, and not-prenascence condition, there is one [result] with not-postnascence; one with not-repetition; one with not-kamma; one with not-resultant; one with not-path; one with not-dissociation …pe….
Ninefold:

with not-root condition, not-predominance condition, not-prenascence condition, not-postnascence condition, not-repetition condition, not-kamma condition, not-resultant condition, not-path condition, and not-dissociation condition—there is one [answer]. (Abbreviated.
Not-Predominance Dyad.

With non-predominance condition, there are three with non-root, two with non-prenascence, three with non-postnascence, three with non-repetition, three with non-kamma, three with non-resultant, three with non-jhāna, three with non-path, and two with non-dissociation. (Abbreviated.
Non-Prenascence Couplets:

With non-prenascence condition, there is one with non-root, two with non-predominance, two with non-postnascence, two with non-repetition, two with non-kamma, two with non-resultant, one with non-path, and two with non-dissociation.

With not-prenascence condition, not-root condition, and not-predominance condition: one; with not-postnascence: one; with not-repetition: one; with not-kamma: one; with not-resultant: one; with not-path: one; with not-dissociation: one. (Abbreviated.
The group beginning with not-postnascence.
With not-postnascence condition ... with not-repetition condition ... with not-kamma condition: in the absence of root, two;

in the absence of predominance, three; in the absence of prenascence, two; in the absence of postnascence, three; in the absence of repetition, three; in the absence of result, three; in the absence of path, two; in the absence of dissociation, two. (Triplet)

With not-kamma condition, not-root condition, and not-predominance condition: two; not-prenascence: one; not-postnascence: two; not-repetition: two; not-resultant: two; not-path: two; not-dissociation: one …pe…. Fivefold Combination:

With not-kamma condition, not-root condition, not-predominance condition, and not-prenascence condition: not-postnascence: one; not-repetition: one; not-resultant: one; not-path: one; not-dissociation: one. (Abbreviated.)

Non-resultant dyad: By way of non-resultant condition, there are two [types] with respect to non-root; three with respect to non-predominance; two with respect to non-prenascence; three with respect to non-postnascence; three with respect to non-repetition; three with respect to non-kamma; two with respect to non-path;
and two with respect to non-dissociation. This concludes the section on non-resultant condition. (It is similar to the section on non-kamma condition.)
The Non-Wisdom Dyad:

With non-wisdom as condition, there are three [results] in the absence of root; three in the absence of predominance; three in the absence of post-nascence; three in the absence of repetition; three in the absence of path …pe…. The Hexad.
With not-jhāna condition, not-root condition, not-predominance condition, not-postnascence condition, and not-repetition condition, there are three [answers] regarding the path. (Abbreviated.
The Path-Duo:

With path condition, there are three [answers] for not-root, three for not-predominance, one for not-prenascence, three for not-postnascence, three for not-repetition, two for not-kamma, two for not-resultant, three for not-jhāna, and one for not-dissociation.

With the path condition, not-root condition, and not-predominance condition: three; with not-prenascence: one; with not-postnascence: three; with not-repetition: three; with not-kamma: two; with not-resultant: two; with not-jhāna: three; with not-dissociation: one …pe…. Fivefold.

With path condition, not-root condition, not-predominance condition, not-prenascence condition, and not-postnascence: one; not-repetition: one; not-kamma: one; not-resultant: one; not-dissociation: one. (Abbreviated. The Non-Dissociation Pair:
With non-dissociation condition, not-root: one; not-predominance: two; not-prenascence: two; not-postnascence: two; not-repetition: two; not-kamma: two; not-resultant: two; not-path: one.
Under the condition of non-dissociation, with the conditions of not-root, not-predominance, not-prenascence, not-postnascence, not-repetition, not-kamma, not-resultant, and not-path: one [state]...
[and so on] ...ninefold.

With non-dissociation condition, not-root condition, not-predominance condition, not-prenascence condition, not-postnascence condition, not-repetition condition, not-kamma condition, not-resultant condition, and not-path condition: one [formula]. (Abbreviated.
Negative Enumeration. 1.3.1.3.
Positive-Negative Conditions.
Hetuduka:

With root condition as the basis, there are three [answers] for non-predominance; two for non-prenascence; three for non-postnascence; three for non-repetition; three for non-kamma; three for non-resultant; and two for non-dissociation. (Tika)

With root condition and object condition, there are three [answers] for non-predominance, two for non-prenascence, three for non-postnascence, three for non-repetition, three for non-kamma, three for non-resultant, and two for non-dissociation.
As with the wholesome triad, so it should be counted.
This is the Positive-Negative (Anuloma-Paccanīya) method.
1.3.1.4. Positive Order of the Negative Condition (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma) The Non-root Pair (Nahetuduka):

With the non-root condition, there are three [results] in the object condition, three in the proximity condition, three in the contiguity condition, three in the conascence condition, and [three] in the mutuality condition.
Three in dependence, three in decisive support, three in prenascence, two in repetition, three in kamma, three in result,
three in nutriment, three in faculty, two in jhāna, one in path, three in association, three in dissociation,
three in presence, three in absence, three in disappearance, and three in non-disappearance.

With the absence of root condition and the absence of predominance condition: three in the object condition, three in the proximity condition, three in the contiguity condition, three in the conascence condition, three in the mutuality condition,
three in the dependence condition, three in the strong-dependence condition, three in the prenascence condition, and two in the repetition condition.
In kamma: three; in resultant: three; in nutriment: three; in faculty: three; in jhāna: two; in path: one; in association: three;
in dissociation: three; in presence: three; in absence: three; in disappearance: three; in non-disappearance: three. (Tetrad)
With not-root condition, not-predominance condition, and not-prenascence condition: one [way] in object; one in proximity; one in contiguity;
one in conascence; one in mutuality; one in dependence; one in strong-dependence;
one in repetition; one in kamma; one in resultant; one in nutriment; one in faculty; one in jhāna; one in path; one in association.
One [condition] by way of dissociation, one by way of presence, one by way of absence, one by way of disappearance, and one by way of non-disappearance …pe… Seven [conditions]:
not-root condition, not-predominance condition, not-prenascence condition, not-postnascence condition, and not-repetition condition.
With not-kamma-condition: one [condition] in object, one in proximity, one in contiguity, one in conascence, one in mutuality, one in dependence,
one in strong-dependence, one in nutriment, one in faculty, one in jhāna, one in association,
one in presence, one in absence, one in disappearance, and one in non-disappearance …pe….
Ten conditions:
not-root condition, not-predominance condition …pe… not-kamma condition, not-resultant condition, not-path condition, not-dissociation condition:
one [way] in the object, one in the immediate, one in the contiguity, one in the conascence;

One with mutuality, one with dependence, one with strong-dependence, one with nutriment, one with faculty, one with jhāna, one with association, one with presence, one with absence, one with disappearance, and one with non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
This concludes the section based on the non-root condition.
Non-predominance dyad:
With non-predominance condition, there are three [results] under the root condition ... pe ... three under the non-disappearance condition. (Abbreviated.
Non-prenascence dyad.
With prenascence condition and root condition, two; ... pe ... with non-disappearance condition, two.

(Abbreviated. The Section on Non-postnascence, etc.: With non-postnascence condition ... non-repetition condition ... non-kamma condition ... non-resultant condition and root condition, three; ... pe ... with non-disappearance condition, three. (Abbreviated.)

The *Najhānaduka*: With the condition of non-jhāna, there are three [results] in the object-condition; three in the proximity-condition; three in the contiguity-condition; three in the co-nascence-condition; three in the mutuality-condition; three in the dependence-condition;
three in the decisive-support-condition; three in the prenascence-condition; three in the kamma-condition; three in the resultant-condition; [three] in the nutriment-condition...
Three for the faculties, three for association, three for dissociation, three for presence, three for absence, three for disappearance, and three for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
[The Non-Path Dyad]

With path-condition as the condition: three in the object, three in the immediate, three in the contiguity … pe … one in repetition, three in kamma … pe … two in jhāna … pe … three in non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
The Non-dissociation Couplets:
With non-dissociation-condition as the condition: two in root, two in object, two in predominance, two in immediate, two in contiguity … pe … [continue as appropriate].
Two in co-nascence, two in mutuality, two in dependence, two in decisive support, two in repetition,
two in kamma, two in result, two in nutriment, two in faculty, two in jhāna, two in path, two in association,
two in presence, two in absence, two in disappearance, and two in non-disappearance.
Under the condition of non-dissociation, excluding the root-condition: one [condition] in the object, one in the immediate, one in the contiguity,
one in the conascence, one in the mutuality, one in the dependence, one in the decisive support, one in the repetition, and one in the kamma.
One in nutriment, one in faculty, one in jhāna, one in path, one in association,
one in presence, one in absence, one in disappearance, one in non-disappearance …pe… The Decad.
With non-dissociation condition, not-root condition, not-predominance condition, not-prenascence condition,
not-postnascence condition, not-repetition condition, not-kamma condition, not-resultant condition, and not-path condition: one [condition] in the object,
one in the immediate, one in the contiguity, one in the conascence, one in the mutuality, one in the support, and one in the decisive support.
One [condition] in nutriment, one in faculty, one in jhāna, one in association, one in presence, one in absence,
one in disappearance, and one in non-disappearance.
This is the negative-positive (paccanīyānuloma) sequence.
The Section on Dependence.
1.3.2. The Section on Co-nascence.
A state associated with pleasant feeling is co-nascent with... [and so forth].
1.3.3. Section on Conditions (Paccayavāra):
Conditioned by a state associated with pleasant feeling … [and so forth] … 1.3.4.
Section on Support (Nissayavāra)
Supported by a state associated with pleasant feeling … [and so on] … 1.3.5.
Section on Conjoined (Saṃsaṭṭha-vāra):
Conjoined with a state associated with pleasant feeling … [and so on] …

1.3.6. Section on Associated States (Sampayuttavāra) A state associated with pleasant feeling is associated with a state associated with pleasant feeling that arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*):
two aggregates associated with pleasant feeling [arise] in association with one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling.
Two aggregates are associated with one aggregate. (Abbreviated.
The Section on Association. 1.3.7.
The Section on Questions.
1.3.7.1. Analysis of the Positive Order of Conditions (Paccayānuloma Vibhaṅgavāra): Root Condition (Hetu)
A state associated with pleasant feeling is a condition for a state associated with pleasant feeling by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*):
roots associated with pleasant feeling are a condition for their associated aggregates by way of the root-condition;
at the moment of rebirth-linking, roots associated with pleasant feeling [are a condition] for their associated aggregates...
Conditioned by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*):
A state associated with painful feeling is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state associated with painful feeling—
the roots associated with painful feeling are a condition, by way of root-condition, for the associated aggregates.
A state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling:
roots associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling are a condition, by way of root-condition, for the associated aggregates;
at the moment of rebirth-linking, [roots] associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling...
The cause is a condition, by way of the cause-condition, for the associated aggregates.
Object:
A state associated with pleasant feeling is a condition, by way of the object-condition, for a state associated with pleasant feeling.

Condition: Having given a gift with a mind associated with pleasant feeling, having undertaken moral discipline, or having performed the Uposatha rite, one reviews it with a mind associated with pleasant feeling.
Having emerged from jhānas associated with pleasant feeling, having emerged from the Path, or having emerged from the Fruit, [one reviews them] with a mind associated with pleasant feeling.

One reviews with the mind. The Noble Ones, with a mind associated with pleasant feeling, review the defilements abandoned that were associated with pleasant feeling, they review the defilements suppressed, and they know the defilements formerly practiced.
[They also review] the aggregates associated with pleasant feeling, [associated with] pleasant feeling...
With a mind associated [with that feeling], one contemplates it as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; one relishes it and delights in it.
Taking that as an object, greed associated with pleasant feeling arises, and wrong view arises.
Taking the aggregates associated with pleasant feeling as an object, aggregates associated with pleasant feeling arise.
A state associated with pleasant feeling is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state associated with painful feeling:

having given a gift with a mind associated with pleasant feeling, having undertaken the precepts, or having performed the Uposatha duties, remorse arises in one who feels regret, and mental grief arises. [Likewise] when a jhāna associated with pleasant feeling has been lost...
In one who feels remorse, mental grief arises. Taking the aggregates associated with pleasant feeling as an object, the aggregates associated with painful feeling arise.
A state associated with pleasant feeling is related to a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

Conditioned by way of object condition: having given a gift, undertaken moral discipline, or performed the Uposatha rite with a consciousness associated with pleasant feeling, one reviews it with a consciousness associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
Having emerged from a jhāna or emerged from a path associated with pleasant feeling, [one reviews it].
Having emerged from the fruit, one reviews with a consciousness associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
Noble ones, with a consciousness associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, review the defilements abandoned in relation to a consciousness associated with pleasant feeling;
they review the defilements suppressed; [they review] the defilements formerly practiced...

They know. One contemplates with a mind associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling the aggregates associated with pleasant feeling as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; one relishes them and delights in them.
Taking that as an object, lust associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, and restlessness arises.
It arises; by means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds (*cetopariyañāṇa*), one knows the mind of one possessing a consciousness associated with pleasant feeling.

The aggregates associated with pleasant feeling are a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives (*pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇa*), the knowledge of the destination according to deeds (*yathākammupagañāṇa*), the knowledge of future states (*anāgataṁsañāṇa*), and for advertence (*āvajjanā*). [Pleasant feeling]...
